Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Horizon Global Investments Third Quarter 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Global Investments' Third Quarter results. Joining me on today's call are David Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Harper.

David Harper: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional fund performance across our strategies relative to peers and benchmarks, where the majority of our funds continued to generate meaningful alpha through precise stock picking and smart allocation decisions.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, David. From a financial perspective, Horizon Global Investments delivered strong results in the third quarter. Our revenue was $3.45 billion, representing a 22% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by significant assets under management expansion and a favorable geographic mix. Our expenses were $2.10 billion, resulting in net income of $850 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives.

To provide more color on this, let me discuss our assets under management in detail, which stands as the foundation of our business at Horizon Global Investments. We closed the quarter at a record $1.28 trillion in AUM, marking a strong 14% rise from the prior quarter and 22% growth compared to last year. This surpassed the industry benchmark, as noted in recent Morningstar flow reports showing top managers averaging about 16% annual gains.

The increase stemmed from several sources: $32 billion in net client inflows, a 25% jump from the previous quarter; $105 billion from favorable market movements; and a $3 billion benefit from currency shifts as the U.S. dollar appreciated against the euro and yen. Stripping out market and FX effects, our organic expansion hit an 8% annualized pace, propelled by enduring institutional commitments and rising retail interest in our ETFs and model portfolios.

Geographically, our AUM reflects a well-diversified global presence, setting us apart from more domestically focused competitors. Here's the quarter-end split:

North America accounts for 58%, or $742 billion, our core market with 18% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter growth. The U.S. led with $680 billion, riding the wave of equity gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, both up more than 12% amid easing inflation and solid earnings. We attracted a record $18 billion in net inflows, especially into our passive ETF offerings like the Horizon S&P 500 UCITS ETF and target-date series, which pulled in over $5 billion from 401(k)s and IRA transfers. Canada saw upticks in fixed-income products as the Bank of Canada eased early. We've used our advanced risk analytics—similar to Aladdin—to secure mandates from major wirehouses like Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley, where advisors seek cost-effective options with ESG features.

Europe makes up 24%, or $307 billion, with 12% annual growth but stability quarter-over-quarter amid ECB hesitancy and lingering UK LDI issues impacting pensions. Continental Europe, at $220 billion, shone with €4.2 billion in inflows to our UCITS sustainable equity funds meeting SFDR Article 8 and 9 standards. Our MiFID II-ready model platform has boosted separately managed accounts via UBS and Deutsche Bank partnerships. In the UK, we shifted to LDI alternatives, up 15% on higher yields, and eye MiCA rules for crypto ETP opportunities through our Digital Asset UCITS ETF.

Asia-Pacific, at 13% or $166 billion, was the standout with 38% yearly and 20% quarterly surges, highlighting our expansion push. China A-shares and Indian equities drew $8 billion in flows to our hedged MSCI China A and Nifty 50 ETFs—double prior quarter levels. Wealth ties with DBS in Singapore and HDFC in India added $3.5 billion from high-net-worth clients amid generational wealth shifts. Japan benefited from GPIF reallocations to our yen-hedged equities. Currency gains from AUD and KRW added $2 billion. Our blockchain custody with State Street cut settlement times 40%, landing sovereign mandates from GIC and Temasek.

The rest of the world, 5% or $64 billion, grew 15% yearly, with Latin America via Brazil BDR ETFs and Middle East infrastructure debt from GCC funds. $2 billion inflows came from our EM local bond strategies handling volatility like Argentina's.

By product, alternatives now at 22% of AUM, up from 18% last year, with private credit and real assets at $180 billion amid a $1.7 trillion U.S. middle-market lending void. ESG AUM reached $420 billion, 33% total, per PRI and TCFD. Our ApexFlow portal with Salesforce drove 30% retail flows, and Asia white-label seeding hit $15 billion. Blended fees dipped just 28 bps, stable year-over-year.

This sets us up for mid-teens growth, ready for the $120 trillion wealth transfer per Cerulli.

Turning to mergers and acquisitions, a vital part of our inorganic strategy this quarter. In an industry with organic growth lagging at 4-5% amid ETF shifts, we've pursued targeted deals for scale, product breadth, and alpha in alternatives and ESG. With global AUM over $120 trillion, up 8% per McKinsey, M&A volumes rose 15% in early 2024 as peers like BlackRock bolt on privates and RIAs.

We completed two deals adding $12.4 billion AUM at 8.2x revenue—below the 11-12x norm. First, $850 million for Pinnacle Wealth Strategies, a top-15 U.S. Southeast RIA with $8.2 billion FUM in HNW mandates. Financed 60% cash from $450 million Q1 free cash, 40% credit at LIBOR+125bps, it accretes 7% to EPS, lifting RIA share to 22%. Pinnacle's 45 bps fees exceed our ETF beta, adding direct indexing and tax overlays for the $2 trillion opportunity per Cerulli.

Synergies: $18 million run-rate savings via OMS/PMS integration, cutting tech costs 25%; 98% retention, 12% cross-sell to ESG ETFs.

Second, $425 million for EuroAlt Partners, London private credit specialist with €3.5 billion AUM. At 7.5x revenue, 70% stock, it makes us top-20 in European debt yielding 9-11% L+400bps. Expect 15% revenue boost from co-mingled funds for Gulf SWFs.

Pro forma: Americas 62%, EMEA 25%, APAC 13%; $200 million to Sydney JV counters Asia RIA outflows. Inorganic added 9.1% growth vs. 3.2% organic, pushing alternatives to 28% (35% FY26 target) amid $17 trillion dry powder per Bain. $50 million in AI diligence and data lake cut integration to 9 months.

Pipeline: $25-30 billion targets, three U.S. LOIs, one EU ESG quant; leverage 1.5-2.0x EBITDA on $2.8 billion cash, BBB+ rating. Drives 12-15% EPS growth in consolidation.

Now, on distribution partnerships and channel expansion, another major driver. Distribution fuels 60% of organic inflows industry-wide per Morningstar; we generated $28.4 billion partnership flows this quarter, up 22% YoY, 45% of $63.2 billion total nets, aiding 8.2% organic growth to $512 billion AUM—wait, aligning with our broader $1.28 trillion total.

Key areas: partnerships, channels, regions, tech.

With Schwab Advisor Services, year three expansion to six ETFs like HLVE ($4.2 billion YTD, 15% low-vol share at 28 bps fees).

RIA deal with Envestnet MoneyGuide: $7.1 billion SMA flows; RIAs now $145 billion AUM, 18% up.

UBS EMEA: $3.8 billion sustainable FI; BlackRock sub-advisory pilot.

Channels: HorizonX direct indexing at $12 billion, 45% QoQ, 120 bps tax alpha; APIs in Tamarac/Orion.

B2C robo with Betterment: $2.9 billion, 65% thematics; advisor portal up 17% conversions.

Regions: NA 68% ($19.3B); APAC 35% up ($5.6B) via DBS (14.2% Asia ex-JP fund); EMEA $3.2B; LatAm $1.1B Itaú.

Tech: $45 million Snowflake data lake, PartnerSync APIs (21-day onboarding), AI personalization (28% cross-sell).

High-margin SMAs (55 bps), alts (72 bps) at 22%; 12% target-date share via Fidelity. FY25: $110-130B flows, RIA/Asia deals. Outpaces T. Rowe, Vanguard.

Raj Singh: Thank you, Emily. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging disciplined active management, proprietary tools, and targeted factor exposures.

As active managers overseeing over $450 billion within our broader platform as of Q3 2023, we're dedicated to superior risk-adjusted outcomes via rigorous stock selection, flexible allocations, and unique alpha sources. Data from Morningstar Direct as of September 30 confirms this: 78% of rated strategies topped benchmarks over three years, 65% beat both benchmarks and peers over five years.

In a tough backdrop of sticky inflation, Fed hikes, and geopolitical strains in Europe and the Middle East, here's the asset class and regional breakdown:

Equities, 55% of AUM: Horizon U.S. Large Cap Growth Fund at 18.4% YTD, +320 bps over S&P 500, 1st percentile of 1,200+ peers. Three-year: 12.1% vs. 9.8%, info ratio 0.72 vs. peer 0.41. Gains from AI/cloud overweight (NVIDIA, Microsoft, ServiceNow: 450 bps), sector bets (tech semis: 180 bps).

International: Global Equity 14.2% YTD, +210 bps MSCI ACWI ex-U.S., top decile of 850. Europe ex-UK 16.8% on Nestlé, ASML. EM Equity 8.5% vs. 7.9% MSCI EM, +150 bps peer median; underweight China, picks in India/Taiwan (TSMC, Infosys).

Fixed income, 30%: Core Bond 4.2% YTD, +90 bps Bloomberg Agg, 12th percentile of 600+. Barbell (short Treasuries, HY corporates): 120 bps; BBB financials (JPM): 80 bps. Sharpe 1.15 vs. 0.92.

Opportunistic HY 11.7%, +250 bps ICE HY, top quintile; credit models on energy credits (Occidental): 300 bps. ABS 6.8% vs. 5.1%, non-agency RMBS.

Alternatives, 15%: PE Vintage 2020 22% IRR, +400 bps Cambridge U.S. PE; SaaS/healthcare exits. Infrastructure 9.5% YTD, +180 bps MSCI World Infra; data REITs, EU renewables.

Multi-asset: Balanced Allocation 10.3%, +140 bps peer median, +200 bps 60/40; glide tweaks minimized banking crisis drawdowns.

Regions: NA 60% outperformance (Mag 7 with 15% non-tech); Europe 25% (luxury: LVMH, Hermès); APAC mixed (Japan small-cap +220 bps, EM derisked to 8% vs. peer 12%).

Peers: Top quartile 72% of 250 strategies on 3-yr per eVestment (vs. BlackRock 68%, Vanguard 55%); Fidelity lags equities. Active share 65%, 1.25% fees.

Drivers: Stock selection 55% equity alpha (Brinson); ML quant on alt data (satellite traffic) +0.20 Sharpe. ESG fund +280 bps MSCI USA ESG. Horizon Analytics 2.0: tracking error 3.2% vs. 4.1%. Aggregate Sharpe 1.08 (peer 0.95), -12% drawdown vs. -15%, 82% positive 5-yr alpha.

Forward: Active in ineff markets (alts +25% YoY to $68B); three Q4 active ETFs (mid-cap value, EM tech). Soft growth: cut cyclicals, add gold/TIPS.

Median 5-yr returns 9.2% vs. 7.8% benchmarks.

David Harper: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes advancing our distribution partnerships, channel expansions, and selective M&A to drive inorganic growth while maintaining our edge in performance.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your AUM growth, particularly the geographic variances?

David Harper: Good question, Alex. As Emily outlined, our $1.28 trillion AUM reflects balanced drivers, with Asia-Pacific surging 38% YoY on $8 billion inflows to China and India products, bolstered by DBS and HDFC ties. North America remains steady at 58% with $18 billion U.S. ETF flows, while Europe held firm despite ECB noise via UCITS ESG. Organic at 8% annualized underscores institutional and retail strength across regions.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. And a follow-up on the impact of your recent M&A deals on near-term margins?

Emily Vargas: Absolutely, Alex. The Pinnacle and EuroAlt acquisitions add $12.4 billion at attractive 8.2x multiples, with Pinnacle already accretive 7% to EPS and $18 million synergies from tech integration. EuroAlt boosts private credit yields to 9-11%, enhancing margins as alts rise to 28%. Client retention at 98% and cross-sell support stable fees amid compression.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Barclays.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Horizon U.S. Large Cap Growth Fund?

Raj Singh: Thanks, Jordan. Our flagship fund returned 18.4% YTD through Q3, outperforming the S&P 500 by 320 basis points and landing in the 1st percentile among over 1,200 Morningstar Large Growth peers. Over three years annualized, it's 12.1% versus the benchmark's 9.8%, with an information ratio of 0.72 exceeding peers. Key contributors were overweights in AI and cloud leaders like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and ServiceNow for 450 bps active return, plus tech semis allocation amid the AI surge.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Harper for closing remarks.

David Harper: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Horizon Global Investments. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
